result.text: Title: Farming Bot Players want to create custom farming bots, that help them gather resources.
First you have to find out which resources you want.
Up to 10 resources in parallel can be collected, some resources are more urgently needed than others.
Some resources are required to create tools that are needed to gather other resources (create a custom logic of the dependencies in your game).
After all preferences are collected, your bot starts farming.
Sometimes, random natural disasters strike and set your bot back.
Whenever some milestones are reached, you are notified.
During farming it is possible to update the list of to be farmed materials (at all times).
After the bot is finished, you should be able to brag to selected friends and/or send them materials.

args.text: When the description distinguishes a human participant from an automated system that performs work on their behalf, model their responsibilities in separate BPMN lanes or pools, and use message flows for communication across pools.

trace.reason: Check existing documented guidance on representing human and automated participants before proposing a collaboration guideline.

result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.

args.text: When a process description assigns activities to both a human user and an automated system acting for them, model those responsibilities in separate lanes within the process unless the description establishes them as independent participants.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already captures this human-versus-automation responsibility distinction.

result.rule: When the description assigns work within one process to both a human user and an automated system acting for that user.: Use separate lanes to show their respective responsibilities and assign each described activity to the responsible lane.

When the description states that a distinct activity occurs between a preceding process stage and a later activity: Model the activity as a separate task and connect it to the preceding and following flow in the stated order.

When the description states that a participant performs a distinct action between other steps: Model the action as its own activity and connect it to the preceding and following steps with sequence flows in the described order.
When the description explicitly requires a human participant to carry out an activity: Model that activity as a user task rather than a generic task.
